items.title: Advancing aging biomarkers and intervention discovery at the TimePie Longevity Forum
items.author: Qingling Yang
items.content: On 20–21 September 2025, the 6th TimePie Longevity Forum convened approximately 2,500 participants from 16 countries in Shanghai. Attendees spanned aging biology, biomarker development and clinical geroscience. The forum’s aim was to bridge mechanistic discoveries with translational applications, with a particular emphasis on biomarker frameworks capable of guiding intervention testing in humans.

items.title: Exercise enhances aged chondrocyte health through microRNA-29-enriched extracellular vesicles
items.author: Fabrisia Ambrosio
items.content: Iijima and colleagues identify a mechanism by which exercise promotes cartilage health through exercise-primed extracellular vesicles enriched in microRNA-29, which restore chondrocyte health and cartilage integrity through epigenetic derepression of KL.

items.title: Mitochondrial membrane lipid cardiolipin controls fiber-type adaptations in aging muscle via estrogen-related receptor γ
items.author: Zachary Gerhart-Hines
items.content: Finger et al. report that declining synthesis of the mitochondrial membrane lipid cardiolipin is a feature of aging in mouse and human skeletal muscle, driving age-related fiber-type and metabolic adaptations through mitochondria-to-nucleus communication.

items.title: A cross-species single-cell kidney epigenome atlas reveals epithelial-dominant aging-like states in disease
items.author: Kun Zhang
items.content: Jeong, Lake and colleagues map changes in the human and mouse kidney DNA methylomes at single-cell resolution across disease and aging, respectively. They identify disease-associated epithelial states with epigenetic age acceleration, altered DNA methylation and chromatin compartments and spatially localized repair programs.

items.title: Multi-modality profiling identifies Neisseria flavescens as a central geroprotective oral commensal in humans
items.author: Jing-Dong J. Han
items.content: Chen, Ren, Zhou, Wang et al. use the generative framework AURORA to link the oral commensal Neisseria flavescens to decelerated aging in humans. In worms and mice, live and heat-killed supplementation, respectively, are geroprotective.
